bullets.title: NVDA CEO crisis dominates tape: Huang ousted, Bessent pushes outside hire, Congress tightens chip exports
bullets.body: Jensen Huang was removed as NVDA CEO amid espionage/national-security concerns before allegations were verified; interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to curb startup/infrastructure financing. Treasury Secretary Bessent publicly called for an external successor, while major shareholders Altimeter and Atreides—plus Elon Musk—are lobbying for Huang's return. Separately, Congress is accelerating bipartisan bills to restrict advanced AI chip exports to China, with MATCH Act revival seen as tail risk for ASML; Commerce Secretary Lutnick faces scrutiny over Cantor Fitzgerald conflicts.

bullets.title: NVDA pre-market -3.5–4.4%; semis broadly down with MU -6.2%, MRVL -6.1%, COHR -7.0%
bullets.body: NVDA opened down 3.5–4.4% with the leadership vacuum and export-control overhang compounding pressure on the entire semiconductor complex. MU fell 6.2%, MRVL -6.1%, AMD -5.3%, INTC -5.3%, AVGO -4.1%; optical/comms names also hit hard with COHR -7.0%, LITE -6.9%, CIEN -5.4%. Crypto and neo-cloud names also fell sharply with BTC down 6.7%, CRWV -6.8%, and BTDR -7.0%.

bullets.title: S&P futures -0.6–0.7%, Nasdaq futures -1.3–1.5% Monday open; 10yr yield 5.14–5.15%, oil ~$88–96
bullets.body: Equity futures are soft Monday morning (S&P -0.6–0.7%, NDX -1.3–1.5%) with the NVDA saga and tighter financial conditions the primary overhangs. The 10-year yield sits at 5.14–5.15% following October's hot CPI print (+0.35% headline, +0.30% core, both ~0.1% above expectations); WTI is around $88/bbl. VIX remains near 5-year lows in positioning terms though options volumes surged (Nov 5 saw largest put volume ever).

bullets.title: Fed repricing hawkish: market pricing 3–3.5 additional hikes to 4.5–4.75%; December hike near-consensus
bullets.body: October core CPI at 0.30% m/m (3.7% 3-month annualized) for the third consecutive above-trend print has firmly shifted the Fed baseline. JPMorgan, Morgan Stanley, and Piper Sandler all expect a December 25bp hike with further hikes in January and March/April, taking rates to 4.5–4.75%. Core PCE tracking 0.30% m/m (3.2% YoY); M2 growth at 5.6% trending toward 7%; consumer inflation expectations reaccelerated to 3.9% in October. Fed rhetoric (Jefferson, Williams) is probing for the disinflationary rate but not committing to December.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley raises S&P 500 YE27 target to 8,700 at 19x forward EPS; JPM holds 8,000
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley lifted its S&P 500 price target to 8,700 (19x forward EPS on $458 2028E), projecting 2026 EPS of $369 (+34%), 2027 of $420 (+14%), and 2028 of $458 (+9%), with the Oct correction to 7,100–7,300 seen as an attractive entry. JPMorgan reiterated 8,000, preferring hyperscalers over high-beta AI and noting conditions for cyclical catch-up are building but missing a declining-inflation piece. SPX 200-day MA support near 7,335.

bullets.title: Goldman 2027 global growth at 2.8%; AI capex rising from $1.1tn to $1.8tn; two Fed hikes then cuts late 2027
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs forecasts 2027 global growth at 2.8% with AI investment rising from $1.1tn to $1.8tn as the primary demand driver, while two more Fed hikes are expected before cuts resume in late 2027. Morgan Stanley's parallel outlook sees global growth solid in 2027–28 but inflation persistently high, with DM central banks entering a modest hiking cycle; the downside scenario involves oil at $125–150/bbl forcing deeper tightening and a mild US recession in late 2027.

bullets.title: AI cycle debate intensifies: bear/bull split on whether NVDA CEO change breaks ecosystem financing model
bullets.body: The core market debate is whether interim CEO Kress and a potential external successor will sustain Nvidia's aggressive pre-commitment model that underpins neoclouds, indie labs, and inference providers—Goldman estimates AI infrastructure financing pullback could remove $50B+ from the ecosystem. Bears (Evercore, 22V) see NVDA P/E compressing toward 8–11x with revenue peaks in sight; bulls (UBS's Arcuri) expect FQ3 beat of ~$3–4B to ~$111–112B and FQ4 guide of ~$130B, with the leadership issue manageable. NVDA '27 revenue seen as largely locked in regardless.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex forecasts intact at $1.6tn 2027 / $1.8tn 2028; 30%+ powered DC shortfall through 2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and Goldman all leave hyperscaler capex forecasts unchanged at ~$1.6tn in 2027 rising to ~$1.8tn in 2028, with AI project finance issuance raised to $545bn from $300bn. A powered data-center shortfall exceeding 30% through 2028 persists; US data-center additions are expected to dip 4% YoY in 2028 before rebounding 38% in 2029. Hyperscalers issued $67B in debt since Sept 30 to fund buildouts, reshaping global credit supply/demand dynamics.

bullets.title: Semis positioning reset 67% from YTD highs; HF selling at 6-week record; AMD/AVGO seen as NVDA beneficiaries
bullets.body: Hedge fund net exposure to US semis fell 67% from YTD highs to the lowest since September 2025, with the long/short ratio declining from 4.4x to 2.1x over six consecutive weeks of selling (longest streak on record). The combined 6-month positioning + price z-score hit nearly -3z—a setup similar to the late-July momentum reset. AMD (+18.9% 5-day) and AVGO (+18% 5-day) are the primary beneficiaries of rotation out of NVDA, while retail bought $1.6B of NVDA on Thursday (10x the next-most-bought name).

bullets.title: Market breadth fragile: QQQ broke 200-day MA; bull/bear ratio at 1.5, lowest since April; semis down 21% since October
bullets.body: QQQ broke below its 200-day moving average and semis are down 21% since October, with eight SOX components now below their 200-day MAs (AMAT, AMKR, FORM, KLAC, LRCX, ONTO, SITM, TER). The Investors Intelligence bull/bear ratio fell to 1.5 (lowest since April, down from 3.8 in September), and fewer than 60% of Russell 3000 stocks are above their 200-day MAs. Credit spreads have failed to confirm the equity bounce, reinforcing rebound-durability concerns. Momentum regime is shifting with AI names migrating from long to short leg of 3m/6m momentum baskets.

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO priced at $70–$78/share ($1.4–1.5tn valuation); 6x oversubscribed with $26B concurrent private placement
bullets.body: Anthropic (ANT) is set to price its 825M-share IPO (97% primary) at $70–$78 per share on Nov 18, implying a ~$1.4–1.5tn valuation on 6x institutional oversubscription. A concurrent $26B Class N private placement accompanies the offering; Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley are joint lead books. The deal is seen as strategically important as Jensen Huang's exit removes an influential open-AI champion, potentially strengthening Anthropic and OpenAI's positions.

bullets.title: October CPI stickiness: 10yr back to 5.15%; rate-sensitive sectors (ITB, XLU) flagged as vulnerable
bullets.body: The hot October CPI print drove the 10-year yield back to 5.15% from 4.86%, with the 2-year rising ~37bps week-over-week and S&P 500 forward P/E de-rating from 23.2x to 18.2x. ITB rallied 25% from October lows but existing-home sales fell to a 16-year low; XLU's 2.75% yield is unattractive vs. 5%+ Treasuries and its correlation to bonds has broken down. MBA mortgage applications fell 40% YoY in October with refinancing down 58%.

bullets.title: JPM derivatives: buy SMH call spreads, sell RTY calls to buy SPX calls; long SPX 2027/28 dividend futures
bullets.body: JPMorgan equity derivatives strategy recommends buying SMH call spreads to position for an AI-momentum rebound with cleaner positioning and year-end tailwinds, selling RTY calls to fund SPX calls (higher rates and sticky inflation favoring large caps), and staying long SPX 2027/2028 dividend futures which price zero growth vs. ~6% realized average. Buy XLP put spreads as a hedge on stretched defensive rotation. Short-dated vol supply from ETFs/0DTE is suppressing VIX but support can fade quickly in sell-offs.

bullets.title: Value/Growth rotation at extremes: Russell 1K Value outperformed Growth by 32% YTM, widest since dot-com
bullets.body: Russell 1000 Value has outperformed Growth by 32% year-to-date, the widest spread since the dot-com bubble, with value now trading at the 97th percentile on 2FY P/E (18.8x) while growth sits at the 48th percentile (19.4x)—reversing the historical premium. Jefferies argues the risk/reward now favors a growth snapback; OPCO technicals show market leadership shifting toward value/defensive/higher-quality but warns <60% of Russell 3000 above 200-day MAs makes any year-end rally participation dangerously narrow.

bullets.title: Software earnings bifurcated: AI leaders beating, tier-2 beneficiaries disappointing; ARR beats at lowest since Q1/25
bullets.body: Q3/26 software earnings showed clear bifurcation with AI leaders (MSFT, PLTR, NET, DDOG, TEAM) beating while tier-2 AI beneficiaries disappointed; ARR/billings beat rate fell to 1.5% vs. 3.4% the prior quarter, the lowest since Q1/25. RBC notes AI spending is taking away budget or delaying decision-making at non-leaders. All-SaaS multiples declined 3.57% week-over-week to 5.6x FY+2 EV/Sales; Wolfe remains long its Agentic Infra basket (SNOW, TWLO, DDOG, NET).

bullets.title: October internet ad spend missed Sept by 50bps; Q4 growth revised down 40bps; GOOGL gaining AI search share
bullets.body: October ad spend growth trailed September by 50bps, prompting a 40bps downward revision to Q4 2026 internet growth estimates. GOOGL is notably gaining AI search share with 25.6% of citations among the top 1,000 domains. Reddit US daily active users declined 12% month-over-month in October, while RBLX October global DAUs were +13% YoY but Q4 is projected at -9% YoY given the GTA VI console launch headwind.

bullets.title: China retail sales soft in October (+0.4% YoY vs +0.8% cons); consumption stimulus and RMB 60tn 2030 target announced
bullets.body: China October retail sales rose just 0.4% YoY (vs. +0.8% consensus, slowing from +1.1% in September) with Gold & Jewelry -28.7% YoY and online retail -1.7% YoY. Seven government departments announced consumption stimulus targeting county-level expansion and RMB 250bn in special bonds for trade-in programs, with a headline target of RMB 60tn in retail sales by 2030. Domestic consumption is expected to remain broadly soft into Q4 2026.

bullets.title: Macro job market strengthening but AI capex inflation at 9.1% YoY exceeds 1970s peak; free cash flows deteriorating
bullets.body: The labor market is broadly healthy—initial claims trending down, October payrolls +159k, 3-month average 137k/month (highest since May)—supporting consumer spending. However, tech equipment capex inflation hit 9.1% YoY, exceeding the 1970s peak of 8.5%, and free cash flows across AI-exposed companies are deteriorating with mounting credit concerns. AI capex is expected to peak in 2026/2027 and slow into 2028, raising questions about the cycle's sustainability.

bullets.title: Upper C-Band auction confirmed for April 2027; JPM estimates $53B total spend with Verizon leading at $15–20B
bullets.body: The FCC released final Upper C-Band auction procedures with bidding starting April 27, 2027, covering 160 MHz across 3,248 flexible-use licenses. JPMorgan maintains its ~$53B total spend estimate ($1.00/MHz-pop); Verizon is expected to bid most aggressively ($15–20B) given its smallest sub-6 GHz position, while SpaceX (up to $10B) is the largest swing factor after its Grain low-band spectrum agreement. Spending is manageable for incumbent balance sheets but could slow Verizon buybacks or deleveraging.

bullets.title: TSMC/Samsung supply chain: HBM4 shortages push GB300 volumes to H1 2027; Samsung winning new US cloud foundry orders
bullets.body: HBM4 shortages could push volume shipments from year-end into H1 2027, with GB300 remaining the primary 2026 Blackwell product. Samsung won new AI chip foundry orders from major US cloud providers for a second straight quarter with commercial shipments expected in 2028, as tight TSMC capacity drives customers to seek a second source. SMIC expects foundry capacity constraints through 2027 and possibly into H2 2028, quoting equipment delivery lead times of 16–24 months.
